parts.title: The Importance of Law
parts.article:
The Importance of Law
 
(A) The law influences all of us virtually all the time. It governs almost all aspects of our behaviour, and even what happens to us when we are no longer alive. It affects us from the embryo onwards. It governs the air we breathe, the food and drink we consume, our travel, family relationships, and our property. It applies at the bottom of the ocean and in space. Each time we examine a label on a food product, engage in work as an employee or employer, travel on the roads, go to school to learn or to teach, stay in a hotel, borrow a library book, create or dissolve a commercial company, play sports, or engage the services of someone for anything from plumbing a sink to planning a city, we are in the world of law.
 
(B) Law has also become much more widely recognised as the standard by which behaviour needs to be judged. A very telling development in recent history is the way in which the idea of law has permeated all parts of social life. The universal standard of whether something is socially tolerated is progressively becoming whether it is legal, rather than something that has always been considered acceptable. In earlier times, most people were illiterate. Today, by contrast, a vast number of people can read, and it is becoming easier for people to take an interest in law, and for the general population to help actually shape the law in many countries. However, law is a versatile instrument that can be used equally well for the improvement or the degradation of humanity.
 
(C) This, of course, puts law in a very significant position. In our rapidly developing world, all sorts of skills and knowledge are valuable. Those people, for example, with knowledge of computers, the internet, and communications technology are relied upon by the rest of us. There is now someone with IT skills or an IT help desk in every UK school, every company, every hospital, every local and central government office. Without their knowledge, many parts of commercial and social life today would seize up in minutes. But legal understanding is just as vital and as universally needed. The American comedian Jerry Seinfeld put it like this, ‘We are all throwing the dice, playing the game, moving our pieces around the board, but if there is a problem, the lawyer is the only person who has read the inside of the top of the box.’ In other words, the lawyer is the only person who has read and made sense of the rules.
 
(D) The number of laws has never been greater. In the UK alone, about 35 new Acts of Parliament are produced every year, thereby delivering thousands of new rules. The legislative output of the British Parliament has more than doubled in recent times from 1,100 pages a year in the early 1970s, to over 2,500 pages a year today. Between 1997 and 2006, the legislature passed 365 Acts of Parliament and more than 32,000 legally binding statutory instruments. In a system with so much law, lawyers do a great deal not just to vindicate the rights of citizens and organisations but also to help develop the law through legal arguments, some of which are adapted by judges to become laws. Law courts can and do produce new law and revise old law, but they do so having heard the arguments of lawyers.
 
(E) However, despite their important role in developing the rules, lawyers are not universally admired. Anti-lawyer jokes have a long history going back to the ancient Greeks. More recently, the son of a famous Hollywood actor was asked at his junior school what his father did for a living, to which he replied, ‘My daddy is a movie actor, and sometimes he plays the good guy, and sometimes, he plays the lawyer.’ For balance, though, it is worth remembering that there are and have been many heroic and revered lawyers such as the Roman philosopher and politician Cicero, and Mahatma Gandhi, the Indian campaigner for Independence.
 
(F) People sometimes make comments that characterise lawyers as professionals whose concerns put personal reward above truth, or who gain financially from misfortune. There are undoubtedly lawyers that would fit that bill, just as there are some scientists, journalists and others in that category. But, in general, it is no more just to say that lawyers are bad because they make a living from people’s problems than it is to make the same accusation in respect of nurses or IT consultants. A great many lawyers are involved in public law work, such as that involving civil liberties, housing and other issues. Such work is not lavishly remunerated and the quality of the service provided by these lawyers relies on considerable professional dedication. Moreover, much legal work has nothing to do with conflict or misfortune, but is primarily concerned with drafting documents. Another source of social disaffection for lawyers, and disaffection for the law, is a limited public understanding of how law works and how it could be changed. Greater clarity about these issues, maybe as a result of better public relations, would reduce many aspects of public dissatisfaction with the law.

analyses.content: 你可能看到段末提到的各种职业和地点想选 i，但这些只是为了证明法律“适用于我们生活的全过程”，而不是在讲不同领域的专业知识。

A段："The law influences all of us virtually all the time. It governs almost all aspects of our behaviour, and even what happens to us when we are no longer alive. It affects us from the embryo onwards. ... It applies at the bottom of the ocean and in space."
这一段通过列举我们从出生前到死亡后、以及生活各方各面的场景，说明了法律无处不在并贯穿我们的一生。
这一段的核心在于对比过去和现在，指出如今普通大众（general population）更容易去参与并真正影响和塑造（shape）法律。
你可能看到开头说法律成为判断行为的标准，但整段的落脚点和对比重点在于“大众影响法律的能力增加”，不要被前半段的铺垫带偏。

B段："Today, by contrast, a vast number of people can read, and it is becoming easier for people to take an interest in law, and for the general population to help actually shape the law in many countries."
这段将IT技术人员的计算机技能与律师的法律理解力进行了并列对比，强调这两种不同领域的专业技能（expertise）同样重要。
你可能看到IT技能想选其他无关选项，但这里的IT只是作为一个参照物，用来引出不同“专业领域”的作用和价值。

C段："In our rapidly developing world, all sorts of skills and knowledge are valuable. Those people, for example, with knowledge of computers... are relied upon by the rest of us. ... But legal understanding is just as vital and as universally needed."
本段开篇明义，并用大量数字（产生几千条新规、立法产量翻倍等）直接证明了法律数量的急剧增长（Growth in laws）。

D段："The number of laws has never been greater. In the UK alone, about 35 new Acts of Parliament are produced every year, thereby delivering thousands of new rules. The legislative output of the British Parliament has more than doubled in recent times..."
你可能看到最后一句讲律师和法官发展法律，但全段前四分之三全在列举新法律的暴增数量，核心主旨是“增长”。
这段通过人们讲“反律师的笑话”以及好莱坞演员儿子的调侃，说明了社会上对律师普遍存在负面看法（not universally admired）。
你可能看到最后提到了西塞罗和甘地，但那是为了平衡前文的负面观感而做的客观补充，整段的引子和主要探讨的现象是大众对律师的负面评价。
E段："However, despite their important role in developing the rules, lawyers are not universally admired. Anti-lawyer jokes have a long history going back to the ancient Greeks."
这段作者为律师辩护，列举了律师做公益、起草文件等事实，指出因为律师靠解决问题赚钱就批评他们是“不公平的（no more just）”。
你可能看到第一句话讲律师把利益置于真相之上，但紧接着作者就用“But”反驳了这种观点，全段的核心是解释为什么批评他们是不公平的。

F段："People sometimes make comments that characterise lawyers as professionals whose concerns put personal reward above truth... But, in general, it is no more just to say that lawyers are bad because they make a living from people's problems than it is to make the same accusation in respect of nurses or IT consultants."

analyses.content: C段："Those people, for example, with knowledge of computers... are relied upon by the rest of us. ... But legal understanding is just as vital and as universally needed."
这是一句非常直接的同义替换，"just as vital" 直接对应 "as important as"，定位准确就能拿分。
原文明确将IT/计算机知识和法律理解力进行了对等比较，指出法律理解力“同样至关重要（just as vital）”。

analyses.content: 原文说没有IT知识社会生活几分钟内就会瘫痪（seize up），紧接着强调法律也同样不可或缺，由此推导出没有法律专家社会也无法有效运转。
你可能觉得这句话太绝对，但在作者将法律与决定社会运转的IT技术并列时，就已经表达了法律对社会运作的决定性保障作用。

groups.contentHtml: Lawyers as professionalsPeople sometimes say that is of little interest to lawyers, who are more concerned with making money. This may well be the case with some individuals, in the same way that some or scientific experts may also be driven purely by financial greed. However, criticising lawyers because their work is concerned with people’s problems would be similar to attacking IT staff or for the same reason. In fact, many lawyers focus on questions relating, for example, to housing or civil liberties, which requires them to have to their work. What’s more, a lot of lawyers’ time is spent writing rather than dealing with people’s misfortunes.

analyses.content: 题目说律师对什么缺乏兴趣（is of little interest），原文对应的表达是律师把个人回报置于“真相（truth）”之上。
题目把“put A above B”灵活替换成了“A is more concerned, B is of little interest”，直接填处于次要地位的名词 truth 即可。
F段："People sometimes make comments that characterise lawyers as professionals whose concerns put personal reward above truth, or who gain financially from misfortune."
F段："There are undoubtedly lawyers that would fit that bill, just as there are some scientists, journalists and others in that category."
题目问还有哪些人可能和个别律师一样受贪婪驱使，原文把科学家、其他人与“记者（journalists）”并列。
题目已经给了“scientific experts”（对应 scientists），你只需要在原文的并列项中挑出剩下的具体职业 journalists，注意保留复数。
题目说批评律师就像出于同样原因攻击IT员工或什么人，原文中与 IT consultants 并列的被攻击对象是“护士（nurses）”。
定位到“IT consultants”后直接往前看，紧挨着的并列职业名词就是答案，千万不要漏写表示复数的“s”。
F段："But, in general, it is no more just to say that lawyers are bad because they make a living from people's problems than it is to make the same accusation in respect of nurses or IT consultants."
题目说这类公益工作要求他们对工作有怎样的态度，原文说这依赖于他们极大的职业“奉献精神/敬业精神（dedication）”。
题目里是“have ____ to their work”，填入名词 dedication 即可，不需要带修饰词 professional，因为题目要求 ONE WORD ONLY。
F段："Such work is not lavishly remunerated and the quality of the service provided by these lawyers relies on considerable professional dedication."
题目说律师大量的时间花在写（writing）什么上，原文对应的是起草（drafting）“文件（documents）”。
“writing”和“drafting”是直接的动作同义替换，抓住其后的宾语 documents 即可，注意必须要写复数。
F段："Moreover, much legal work has nothing to do with conflict or misfortune, but is primarily concerned with drafting documents."
